content.user_title: Build Modern C++ Code With Expert Guidance
content.value_statement: Modern C++ work can fail when ownership, templates, and concurrency rules are unclear. This skill guides design, implementation, testing, and performance review.
actual_capabilities: Guides modern C++11 through C++23 feature use.
Explains RAII, smart pointers, and ownership choices.
Provides patterns for templates, concepts, and perfect forwarding.
Covers concurrency with atomics, locks, futures, and coroutines.
Includes CMake, testing, sanitizers, benchmarks, and profiling guidance.
Helps review performance topics such as move semantics, allocators, SIMD, and cache layout.
limitations: It does not compile or run code by itself.
Examples must be adapted to the target compiler, platform, and project rules.
It needs project context for accurate API, ABI, and build decisions.
It does not replace security, safety, or performance validation on real workloads.

use_cases.title: Implement Safer Application Code
use_cases.description: Use the skill to design ownership, resource cleanup, and exception-safe control flow before implementation.

use_cases.title: Design Reusable Library Interfaces
use_cases.description: Use template, concept, and const-correctness guidance to create clearer APIs with compile-time checks.

use_cases.title: Review Performance-Critical Paths
use_cases.description: Use allocator, move semantics, cache layout, SIMD, and benchmark guidance to focus optimization work.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize a Small Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C++ function for RAII, const correctness, smart pointer use, and simpler STL alternatives. Explain each recommended change.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Class Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Help design a modern C++ class for this responsibility. Include ownership rules, exception guarantees, copy and move behavior, and test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Concurrency Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this concurrent C++ design for data races, lock ordering, memory ordering, and lifetime problems. Propose a safer implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Hot Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this performance-critical C++ path. Consider profiling, move semantics, allocation strategy, cache layout, SIMD, and benchmark methodology.

output_examples.input: A request to modernize code that manually manages memory.
output_examples.output: A review that identifies ownership boundaries, recommends RAII wrappers, explains smart pointer choices, and lists tests for cleanup behavior.

output_examples.input: A request to evaluate a multithreaded queue design.
output_examples.output: A concurrency assessment covering synchronization, lifetime, condition variable use, race risks, and a practical validation plan.

output_examples.input: A request to improve slow vector-processing code.
output_examples.output: A performance plan that separates measurement, allocation changes, cache-friendly layout, algorithm choices, and benchmark checks.

best_practices: Provide compiler version, C++ standard, platform, and build system details before asking for code changes.
Ask for tests, sanitizer checks, and benchmark criteria when correctness or speed matters.
State ownership, lifetime, thread-safety, and exception-safety requirements explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad rewrites without sharing constraints, tests, or project style rules.
Do not optimize before defining the measured workload and acceptable tradeoffs.
Do not copy examples into production without adapting error handling, portability, and validation.

faq.question: Can this skill write production C++ code?
faq.answer: It can guide and draft production-oriented code, but you must compile, test, and review it in your environment.

faq.question: Which C++ versions does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers modern C++ from C++11 through C++23, including concepts, ranges, coroutines, and smart pointers.

faq.question: Does it help with build systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes CMake guidance, compiler warnings, sanitizers, static analysis, tests, and benchmark setup.

faq.question: Can it debug concurrency problems?
faq.answer: It can analyze common race, lock, lifetime, and memory-ordering issues when you provide the relevant code and constraints.

faq.question: Can it optimize performance automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest profiling and optimization steps, but real performance claims require measurement on the target workload.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
